subject: chimpanzee
title: Chimpanzees Hunted One Forest's Monkeys Down by 89 Percent

scenes.text: Chimpanzees nearly emptied a forest of monkeys. It took teamwork.
At Ngogo, in Uganda, chimps hunt red colobus monkeys high in the treetops.
Their hunts there succeed about four times out of five.
In Ivory Coast, chimps split up the job: drivers push the monkeys, others block, others wait in ambush.
At Ngogo, red colobus numbers fell about 89 percent between 1975 and 2007, mostly from chimp hunting.
Our closest relative doesn't just eat fruit. It runs ambushes.

description:
Chimpanzees at Ngogo, Uganda, are among the most successful primate hunters ever studied.
Their red colobus hunts succeeded about 78 to 82 percent of the time, and a 33-year census found red colobus there declined by about 89 percent from 1975 to 2007, mainly because of chimpanzee predation. In Tai forest, Ivory Coast, chimps hunt in coordinated groups with drivers, blockers, chasers and ambushers.
Did you know chimps hunted like this?
